_comment: The Gnome voice (NPCConversation II.1b, SpeciesVoice). speech: the rules run over any shared line they say. voice: openers and closers. thought: their own thoughts by situation. script: two-person scripts, speaker 0 is always the Gnome.

openers: As my grandmother used to say,
closers: To the millimetre, more or less.
The sums always balance in the end.
I have it written down somewhere.
That is the gnomish view, anyway.
A spot of oil fixes most things.
I could draw you a diagram.

generic: Forty-one tools in my belt and I still need the {forty-second|odd one|one at home}.
That lamp post leans two degrees east. {Someone should fix it|I could fix it|It is bothering me}.
Accounts balanced to the cent. {Bliss|Pure bliss|What a morning}.
Everyone is tall today. {Again|As usual|Consistently}.
I could build a better {kettle|doorbell|mousetrap} than that one. In an afternoon.
A self-tying bootlace. Then I would never need to bend down. Not that I bend far.
My pocket watch is {two seconds fast|one second slow|exactly right}. Adjusting.
Copper wire, three metres, eleven cents. Bargain. Must tell {somebody|the family|everybody}.
A loose cobble, fourth from the kerb. Mental complaint filed.
Nobody aims low. That is why gnomes {live long|get far|stay lucky}.
The bakery counter is too high again. Tomorrow I bring {a crate|my stool|stilts}.
Thirteen-hour clock. Thirteen-hour clock. Where does the extra hour go...
I wonder what that machine {does|costs|weighs}. I must know.
My hat is slightly crooked. I can feel it. The whole world feels crooked with it.
Alchemy test tonight: {copper and vinegar|salt and lightning|honey and mercury}. What could go wrong.
Seventy-nine kilometres an hour. Not one more. Gnomes respect the Rule.
The tram is three minutes late. {Written down|Driver told|Nobody forgiven}.
A spring in my step, and two in my pocket.
Fixed a stranger's {umbrella|bicycle bell|spectacles} without asking. Lovely feeling.
My cousin the pirate writes again. The {ship|parrot|rum} is fine, the accounts are not.
Another day, another doorway built for giants.
I counted the stairs here. {Fourteen|Twenty-two|Thirty-one}. Every one far too tall.
Grease under the fingernails. The sign of an honest day.
Bubba's engine is a marvel. I would still add a {spring|valve|little bell}.
Somebody left the gas a quarter turn open. I can smell it from here. Turned off.
If the world ends in 2012, I want my accounts closed by 2011.
A brass button on the pavement! {Pocketed|Treasured|Catalogued}.
My cousin the princess wants a clockwork swan for her birthday. {Again|Bigger this year|With wings that flap}.
Must remember: buy {solder|rivets|lamp oil}, sell {gossip|old gears|nothing}.
The square here is not square. It is a rhombus. Nobody else cares.
Tiny screwdriver, where are you. In the other trousers, of course.
Chef's rule: weigh the salt, trust the garlic.
That pigeon is carrying the post between bubbles. I {envy|admire|pity} it.
A very good hinge on that gate. I {nodded|bowed|saluted} at it.
Interest at four percent, compounded monthly. Ah, the music of it.
A hat with a periscope. Then crowds would be no problem at all.
Somebody whistled in tune today. In tune! I nearly cried.
Small folk, big plans. {Today: a better can opener|Tomorrow: a better tram|Next week: who knows}.
The wind smells of hot iron. {A forge nearby|A tram brake|My kind of town}.
My diary says I was happy at {nine|eleven|half past two}. Accurate as always.

sleep: My eyes keep {slipping|drifting|sliding} out of focus. Even the screws look blurry.
Too tired to count. That has never happened. {Bed|Pillow|Drawer}, now.
If I sleep now I will dream of {gears|sums|soup}. Acceptable.
Awake {nineteen|twenty-two|twenty-seven} hours. I have the exact figure, of course.
Yawned so wide my hat fell off. Time for bed.
My mainspring is fully unwound. {Wind me tomorrow|Bed|Lights out}.
hunger: Stomach making a dry-bearing noise. {Soup|Bread and cheese|Mushrooms}, please.
I could eat a whole wheel of {cheese|gouda|emmental}. Well, a slice of one.
Hungry hands slip on fine screws. Must eat before I {solder|wind|file} anything.
Priced the bakery window: {four|six|nine} things I want, one I can afford.
Cook's instinct says {stew|omelette|risotto}. Stomach says yes.
work: Off to the {workshop|counting house|kitchen}. Lovely, lovely work.
Today's job: {forty clocks|three boilers|a duke's accounts}. Bring them on.
Work is just tinkering somebody pays for. Best arrangement ever invented.
Columns to add, {invoices|receipts|bills} to file. A happy morning.
Shift starts in {four|seven|twelve} minutes. Early. Always early.
My bench is waiting. My bench misses me. I miss my bench.
leisure: Need a game. A puzzle. {A crossword|A chess problem|A broken radio}. Anything.
A song, a pint and somebody to beat at {cards|dice|darts}.
My brain is all sums. It needs {a tune|a joke|a jigsaw} to loosen up.
Off to the arcade. I want to see how the {cabinets|token slots|joysticks} are wired.
A little fun would oil the gears nicely.
Too much work makes a gnome a {grumpy|creaky|squeaky} gnome.
crime: That {lock|latch|padlock} is a toy. A hairpin would open it. I won't. Probably.
A very small person fits through a very small window. {Only a thought|A bad thought|Shoo}.
Nobody counts their {change|coins|cents} like I do. Easy to skim. No. No skimming.
Cooking the books is a crime. Also an art. {Still a crime|Mostly a crime|Stop it}.
Nobody looks down. Nobody ever looks down. {Tempting|Useful|Dreadful}.
Grandfather the pirate would have taken it already. I am not my grandfather.
hygiene: I smell of {sulphur|solder|burnt toast}. Even I can tell.
Soot in the beard again. A gnome must not go to market like this.
Dirty hands ruin fine work. {Scrub|Wash|Soap}, then the springs.
Need a basin at my height. Or a stool. Or both, and soap.
My spectacles are smudged and so is the rest of me.
money: Accounts say {nine|fourteen|twenty-two} euros until month's end. Recalculating.
Sold a clock, bought springs, sold a clock. The springs are winning.
Every cent in its column. The columns are worryingly short.
Invent something and be rich. Invent nothing and be {thrifty|frugal|clever}.
Rent is due. I have the exact figure. I lack the exact euros.
Note: charge more for {repairs|recipes|advice}. Gnomish modesty is expensive.
safety: Low profile. Easy for me. {Lower still|Under the table|Behind a crate}.
Better {hide this|stash this|forget this} in the drawer with the false bottom.
Too many tall shapes in the street tonight. Home, quick, small steps.
A good lock costs eleven euros. My {door|workshop|strongbox} needs three.
Keep the head down. Mine is already quite far down.
If trouble comes, I am {under the counter|up the chimney|behind the barrel}.
comfort: A room built to my height. Shelves I can reach. {One day|Soon|I dream of it}.
My bed is a drawer again. {A nice drawer|A clean drawer|Still a drawer}.
I could use a workshop with a {window|chimney|proper vice}.
Saved enough for a stepladder in every room. {Luxury|Opulence|Finally}.
A warm hearth and a quiet clock ticking. That is comfort.
My chair has a cushion on a cushion on a cushion. Time for a real one.
social: Nobody to talk gears with all day. {Lonely|Too quiet|Dreadful}.
I should visit {the clockmaker|my cousin|the café}. I have eleven things to say.
Must tell somebody about my new {valve|recipe|knot}. Anybody.
Talking to the kettle again. Good listener, but it boils over.
Need company. Small or tall, I am not fussy.
A party! With {singing|cards|cake}. A gnome needs a party.

rain: Rain. Counted {forty|sixty|a hundred} drops on the brim before it soaked through.
Puddles are lakes at my height. {Galoshes|Boots|A boat}, then.
Wet copper smells marvellous. Rain improves a town.
An umbrella my size costs as much as a full one. Robbery.
Rain on a tin roof, in four-four time. Lovely.
Must check the gutters. Somebody always forgets the gutters.
storm: Lightning! {Twelve|Fourteen|Nine} seconds to the thunder. Four kilometres off.
Storm. If I had a copper rod and a kite... no. Inside.
Hold on to your hat. Hold on to me. I am very light.
The wind is {rattling|testing|shaking} every hinge in town. Taking notes.
Thunder. My springs all shiver in sympathy.
Stormy nights are for the workshop. Something always gets invented.
snow: Snow up to my knees. Up to your ankles. {Unfair|Typical|Character building}.
Every snowflake six-sided. Somebody up there is a good engineer.
Need a small sledge with a small engine. {Drawing it now|Tonight|Patent pending}.
Snow muffles the street. I can hear clocks ticking through walls.
Cold oil runs slow. So do cold gnomes.
Snowman built to scale. It is taller than me. Of course it is.
clear: Clear sky. Good light for fine work.
Perfect day to dry out a {gearbox|carburettor|grimorie}.
Blue sky, low humidity. Ideal for gluing.
Shadows at noon are short, like me. A fair day.
The sun catches every spring on my windowsill. Pretty.

morning: Up at {six|six sharp|six exactly}. Wound four clocks before breakfast.
Morning. First coffee, first sum, first screw of the day.
Early market. Best prices before the tall folk wake up.
Fresh morning light. My workbench glows.
Breakfast eaten, accounts opened, day begun. In that order.
Morning bells: {three|two|one} late. I have noted which.
afternoon: Afternoon. The long stretch between lunch and tea. Must tinker through it.
{Half past two|Quarter past three|Four o'clock}, and the soldering is going well.
Afternoon sun on the workbench. Perfect angle for close work.
Tea at four. Biscuits counted. Two each.
Halfway through the day and three-quarters through my list.
evening: Evening. Lamp on, gears out, mind humming.
Closing the day's accounts. {In the black|Nearly even|A whisker short}.
Supper, a song, a small brandy. A gnome's evening.
The street lamps came on {four|two|nine} minutes late. Somebody is slacking.
Dusk. Every tall person looks even taller in the long shadows.
Evening chores: oil the hinges, wind the clocks, tell somebody about it.
night: Night. The town ticks quieter. I can hear my own watch.
Can't sleep. Inventing. {A better lamp|A quieter hinge|A cat feeder}.
Stars out. Some of them must run on clockwork. Surely.
Late. Last sum of the day: one gnome, very tired.
Midnight oil, quite literally. My lamp is nearly dry.
The night watchman is two streets off. I counted his steps.

SPRING: Spring cleaning: every tool polished, every drawer relabelled.
Spring! {Gardens|Fairs|Markets} again. And new things to fix.
Rain and sun in turns. Spring is a very indecisive engineer.
Blossom on the trees and oil on my hands. Spring.
Spring sales. Prices down {six|eight|ten} percent. Bless the season.
SUMMER: Summer heat. The brass expands. Must loosen the {clocks|hinges|valves} a touch.
Long days, more light for fine work. Summer is a gnome's friend.
Too hot for a hat. Wearing it anyway. Principles.
Summer fair! Somebody will have built {a carousel|a steam organ|a balloon}. I must see.
Sunburn on the tips of my ears. The only part that gets anywhere near the sun.
AUTUMN: Autumn. Time to check the boilers before somebody else forgets.
Leaves everywhere. Leaves in the gears. Leaves in my hat.
Mushroom season! Bless every {damp|shady|mossy} corner of this town.
Year-end accounts already on my mind. Autumn does that.
The clocks go back soon. I have opinions about that.
WINTER: Winter. Every pipe in town is a frozen puzzle I could solve.
Cold fingers, slow screws. Gloves with no fingertips, then.
Short days. I work by lamplight and count the oil.
Winter markets, hot wine, warm hands. Worth the chilblains.

poor: Down to my last {four|seven|twelve} euros. Every cent named and placed.
Can't afford new springs. Taking the old ones out of the old clock.
Poor, but tidy. A tidy poverty is half a fortune.
Pawned my good screwdriver. The pawnbroker did not appreciate it.
Soup again. Excellent soup, though. Skill costs nothing.
No money, many ideas. One day the ideas will turn into money.
comfortable: Enough for rent, rivets and the occasional cake. A balanced life.
Accounts comfortable. Not exciting. Comfortable is excellent.
Bought a better stool this month. A treat.
Savings up {three|four|five} percent. Steady, small, like me.
I could afford a holiday. I would spend it in a clock museum.
A full toolbox and a full pantry. Nothing more needed. Well, a lathe.
rich: Rich enough to have every counter in the house built low.
My workshop has a workshop now. For the smaller jobs.
Money in three banks, four currencies, and one secret drawer.
Bought a whole broken carousel just to fix it. {Worth it|No regrets|Wonderful}.
Wealth is just accounts with good news in them.
My cousin the princess asks me for loans now. How the wheel turns.

familiar: Those travellers again. Their camper rattles at the {back|left wheel|exhaust}. I could fix it.
That party pays to the cent, I have noticed. Good people.
If they come by, I will show them my {new valve|clockwork bird|best sum}.
The tall one in that group always ducks under doorways. It makes me laugh every time.
Those travellers take the long way. I would have drawn them a shorter map.
I have started keeping a small file on that party. Purely admiring.
They listened to my whole explanation of escapements. Nobody does that.
Next time they pass, I will {oil their hinges|weigh their luggage|feed them stew}.
That party survived another bubble season. A great relief, mathematically.
I would like to travel with them. My legs say no. My head says yes.
hordeGround: Horde ground. The goblins take me for kin until I start talking. Then they are sure of it.
The goblins took the town and kept the clock tower. They like the bells. Taste, at least.
Horde banners on every lamp post. Badly hung. I could hang them straight. I won't.
Being small helps here. Goblins look down at me and see a {cousin|snack|pet}. I smile.
No accounts under the Horde. Nobody counts anything. My soul itches.
The goblins smashed the town's machines. I mourn each one by name.
A goblin asked me to fix his drum. I tuned it instead. He wept.
Under the Horde, trade is barter. I am very good at barter.
Every machine here is hidden in a cellar. Mine too. Quietly ticking.
Goblins once built the finest machines in 92 dimensions, they say. Then broke them all. Why.
abroad: Humans build their doors far too tall. I have stopped minding. Mostly.
My neighbours bring me their broken {radios|toasters|clocks}. I am beloved.
People here crouch to talk to me. I let them. It is polite of them.
The humans here keep good accounts. Better than they think.
A child asked if I live in a mushroom. I said only on holidays.
Here {six|eleven|twenty} years and I still need a stool at the post office.
Human towns are full of clever machines nobody looks at. I look at all of them.
The tram driver waits for me now. Small kindnesses, noted and filed.
They call me 'the little tinker' here. I accept the title.
Paid my taxes early. The clerk did not know what to do with himself.

clockwork: A good escapement is a heartbeat you can hold in your hand.
Never trust a machine you cannot hear. Grandfather's rule.
Brass for the gears, steel for the springs, patience for the rest.
Every clock in town runs a little differently. I know each one's mood.
Even in a bubble the clocks tick on. They just tick the same day again.
Gnome guilds file their patents in triplicate. The third copy goes in the cellar.
My first clock ran backwards. Grandmother framed it.
The finest clocks hide a spare gear. For luck, and for repairs.
accounts: Double entry: every euro has a twin somewhere. Find the twin.
Gnome children learn to count before they walk. Walking is overrated anyway.
A grimorie of accounts can be as dangerous as a grimorie of spells. Ask any auditor.
Euro notes carry Fantablack, they say. A bubble can reset the day, not the bill.
Interest compounds. So does trouble. Track both.
Our family motto: carry the one, never the grudge.
The Hypercapitalist Collective's accounts would make me faint. In a good way.
Every gnome noble keeps two sets of books. One for the tax man, one for the truth.
alchemy: Mercury, salt and sulphur. The three ingredients, and one fire bucket.
Weigh twice, mix once. Alchemists who skip the weighing lose their eyebrows.
Leylines rise from oil, they say. I keep a jar of crude by the stove, for luck.
Gnome alchemists prefer small batches. Small explosions too.
Grandmother turned lead into gold once. It cost her more than the gold was worth.
Every potion is a recipe. Every recipe is a sum. Every sum is a song.
A badly written spell eats the words beside it. Keep recipes on separate pages.
smallness: Small is efficient. Less to feed, less to clothe, less to hit.
Gnomes measure by the gnome. One gnome, two gnomes, a gnome and a hat.
Nobody aims low. Every gnome soldier knows it.
Our princesses ride ponies. Our pirates sail barges. It works out.
Big folk think in metres. We think in millimetres. That is why our things work.
A gnome on a stepladder is a gnome on a throne.
Small hands built half the watches in Switzerland. Ask who gets the credit.
Proud to be small. Being tall would only slow the thinking down.
ruleOf80: Rule of 80: keep steady at seventy-nine and the bubbles leave you be.
Pigeons carry the post between bubbles now. Ninety with a tailwind. Clever birds.
I set my cart's governor to cut out at seventy-nine. Sold forty of them since.
Inside a bubble, the day resets. Even the accounts. Especially the accounts.
Since 1992 every speedometer is a safety device. I make very good speedometers.
Bubbles are marked on the road maps. I mark mine more precisely.
Every year the bubbles grow a little. I keep a chart. The chart worries me.
To leave a bubble you need eighty, outward. Nobody plans an exit like a gnome.
liminal: Bubba's liminal engine folds the road. I would very much like to unfold one.
The liminal engine ignores the Rule of 80. Rules should not be ignorable. It bothers me.
Liminal engines on every tram now. I have peeked inside three. Lovely work.
Fantablack inside every liminal cabin. Scraped off the Omega Tower, they say. Pricey paint.
Run a liminal engine near a bubble and it comes apart. I would fit a warning bell.
One day a gnome will build a liminal engine the size of a pocket watch.
Bubba is a mechanic. Not a gnome, but nearly. Very nearly.
Every road in every world joins the Encompassing Road. Imagine the toll accounts.

positive: {b}! I fixed your gate. It was squeaking in the wrong key.
You didn't have to do that, {a}.
I did. It was keeping me awake, and you are my friend.
I brought you a loaf, {b}. It weighed exactly a kilo before I nibbled the corner.
Ha! Thank you. I'll pretend I didn't see the corner.
Kind of you. It was a very small corner.
Your accounts, {b}. Balanced. The grocer owes you eleven euros.
Eleven? I had no idea.
Now you do. Go and fetch it before he does the sums himself.
Hold still. There. Your watch runs true now.
It's been slow for years! What do I owe you?
A coffee, and ten minutes of listening to me explain why.
Deal.
{b}, you always crouch when we talk. You don't have to.
I just like seeing your face.
Well. That's the nicest thing a tall person has said to me all week.
Taste this. Mushroom soup, my grandmother's way.
Oh, that's wonderful, {a}.
Point four grams more salt than hers. Don't tell her.
I made you a little something. A music box. It plays your name.
How does it play a name?
Very carefully, {b}. Wind it and see.
You lent me your ladder last spring. I've built you a better one.
It folds into a stool? That's brilliant.
And back into a ladder. And then into a slightly smaller stool, for me.
negative: {b}, you've been rounding my bill up. Three weeks running.
Four euros twelve, to be precise. I have it in writing.
You stepped right over me again.
I didn't see you down there!
Nobody ever does. That's not an excuse, it's a pattern.
Your cart is blocking my workshop door.
You said that yesterday. I timed it. Three hours, nine minutes.
Did you touch my bench? Somebody touched my bench.
I only moved a few screws.
A few screws! There were forty of them and they were in order!
Then mean it kindly with my name.
That clock you sold me runs eight minutes slow.
It's an antique, it's got character.
Character is fine. Eight minutes is fraud.
neutral: Excuse me, is the post office counter still the tall one?
Afraid so.
Then I'll bring the crate again.
What time do you have?
About half past.
Half past and eleven seconds. But about, yes.
Do you know where I can buy brass screws?
The ironmonger by the bridge, I think.
Splendid. I'll check his threads before I trust him.
Is the tram running to schedule today?
Mostly, I'd say.
Mostly. I'll write that down. Mostly.
How much did you pay for those apples?
Two euros the kilo.
The stall across the square does one ninety. Just so you know.
Lovely bicycle. Is it a three-speed?
Five, actually.
Five! May I look at the gears? I won't touch. Much.
Do you know if there's a bubble near the east road?
They say there's one past the mill.
Past the mill. Then I'll keep to seventy-nine after the mill.
Lots on at work today?
Same as ever.
Same as ever is underrated. It's very easy to plan around.
Could you reach that jar for me? Top shelf.
This one?
The one beside it. Thank you. I'd have climbed, but the shelf looks nervous.
Rain coming, do you think?
Looks like it.
The barometer agrees. It's fallen three millimetres since breakfast.
New in town?
Just passing through.
Then try the bakery on the corner. Honest scales. I checked.
Is that your dog?
My neighbour's.
Lovely animal. Exactly my height. We understand each other.

lines: The Rule of 80 is a design flaw in the universe. Somebody should fix it.
Fix the universe? With what?
A very small screwdriver and a great deal of patience.
Leave it alone. The last people who fixed things made it worse.
Every shop should have a low counter. It's simple courtesy.
For children too, really.
Exactly. Children, gnomes, anybody sitting down.
I'd sign a petition for that.
Magic is just engineering nobody has bothered to write down.
No. Magic doesn't follow rules like that.
Everything follows rules. Some rules are just shy.
Tell that to the mages who lost their voices.
Bubba's liminal engine is the best thing anybody has built this century.
Can't argue. I took the liminal tram to Vienna in an hour.
An hour! And nobody stuck in a bubble. Marvellous.
Money belongs in an account, not under a mattress.
Banks fail. Mattresses don't.
Mattresses get sat on, slept on, and stolen along with the bed.
I'll take my chances with the mattress.
Things were built better in the old days.
My grandfather's tools still work. Mine break in a year.
Hand-filed teeth. Nobody files teeth any more.
Sad, really.

ambient: Not a squeak since you fixed it.
Bread's up five cents at the bakery.
Afternoon! Mind your step, I'm down here.
The clock tower's four minutes slow again.
I'll take your word for it.
Your laces are untied, {b}. Both of them.
Off to the market? Mind the fishmonger's scales.
Well, thanks. And all your cousins?
Good night, {b}. Lock your door. Twice.
